function: Adversarial evasion-attack detection: learned classifiers label received pilots benign or adversarial and block them before a DL beam predictor; a security function outside the seven areas (p. 5).
notes: Reason function, p. 5. The title on p. 1 matches the DOI. The learned method proposed is X-ZeroSec, an adversarial-input detector built from tree-based classifiers (a direct detector, a second detector trained on TreeSHAP attributions, and a stacking meta-model): p. 5: "detection methodology to filter out adversarial data"; p. 6: "employs a light ML model to classify received signals as either benign or adversarial". It does not design or select beams: p. 13: "detection operates purely as a pre-filter ahead of the existing beamforming pipeline"; p. 15: "without requiring modification of the underlying DLBF model". The DL beam predictor (six fully connected layers, DeepMIMO O1 and CM6) is the attacked model reproduced from Alkhateeb et al. [35], p. 7: "closely follows the methodology outlined by Alkhateeb et al. [35]", so learned beamforming appears only as the application being protected. The main metrics are detection metrics, p. 9: "main performance metrics: detection accuracy on previously encountered (seen) attacks", with achievable rate shown only as the effect of the filter (Figs. 6, 14, 17, 20). Detecting adversarial perturbations of received pilots is a physical-layer security task, like physical-layer authentication, and is not one of the seven areas. above_phy was considered and not applied: the detector classifies physical-layer received pilot signals (pp. 4-6), although it runs as an xApp, p. 17: "operating within the Near-Real-Time RIC". If the reviewer counted the reproduced beam predictor as the learned method, the work would fall in area 3.
